question: Does the FAR limit apply if I finish my attic into living space without changing the outside of the house?

Zone A's development standards table sets the FAR limits. These are 55%, 50% or 45% of lot area, depending on lot size. A footnote to that table creates the exception:

> In order to encourage development within the existing building envelope instead of building outwards or upwards, the floor area ratio standard is not applied to finishing an area into habitable space if: (1) there is no expansion of the exterior building envelope; and (2) the owner has not obtained a final inspection within the prior three years on a building permit issued for an expansion of the building envelope.

(§17.20.040, footnote to the floor area ratio row)

The same footnote appears in the Zone E standards (§17.28.040). If you aren't sure which zone you're in, check your parcel.

So the code allows the FAR standard to be skipped only if both conditions are met. Not changing the outside covers condition (1). Condition (2) looks back three years. If a building permit for an addition was finaled in that window, the exception is not available.

**Code says**

The attic still counts as floor area once it is finished. The code's definition of floor area includes:

> living space on all levels, including within a basement or attic;

(§17.90.020, "Floor area of a building")

This means the finished attic would count toward your floor area. The footnote only says the FAR *standard* is not applied to that conversion.
